guard: the per-principal subject record refuses every state its own writer cannot produce, and never conflates a record that is MISSING with one that reads zero
why: An absent record means this principal never published, so a tip may be recovered from the session
logs beside it. A record that READS ZERO is what abandonment writes after a channel purge, and
recovering into that one silently undoes the abandonment and restores an expectation the subject
no longer has. Missing and zero are different states, and this is the second place in this plane
where conflating them is the defect rather than a nicety.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY, checked rather than assumed: the suite imports ../src/subject-frontier.js by
relative source path, and imports nothing else from this repository. No dist, no build step.
NOT PROVED HERE: that a real publish takes its expectation from this record. That needs a broker
and is graded by smoke:agui-multi-session and its own config.
NOT PROVED HERE, AND NAMED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. The recovery scan opens each log with
O_NOFOLLOW behind the lstat refusal, to close the window between the check and the open. No
cell here can drive that race, and no mutation is registered against the flag, because a
mutant that survives and gets explained away is worse evidence than an absence stated plainly.
The flag is also absent on Windows, which is why the refusal is decided by the lstat and not
by the flag: a guard that evaporates on one platform is not a guard, it is a platform note.

mutations.name: S5 recover a tip into a record that READS zero, not only into an absent one
mutations.find: return new FileSubjectFrontier(path, { v: d.v, space: d.space, principal: d.principal, tip: d.tip });
mutations.replace: return new FileSubjectFrontier(path, { v: d.v, space: d.space, principal: d.principal, tip: d.tip || (await FileSubjectFrontier.recoverTipFromThreadLogs(dirname(path), opts.principal)) });
mutations.note: The tempting simplification: treat a zero tip as 'nothing yet' wherever it appears. It reads as a tidy-up and it undoes an abandonment.

mutations.name: S7 an unreadable sibling log is skipped instead of refused
mutations.find: throw new SubjectFrontierCorruptError(walPath, "a readable thread log while recovering the subject tip", (e as Error).message);
mutations.note: Skipping under-counts the tip, which does not fail here. It fails later, permanently, with a message about a moved subject tip that points at everything except the file quietly ignored.

mutations.name: S10 a symlinked thread directory is followed instead of refused
mutations.note: The create path refuses a symlinked component, so the recovery path following one puts the guard on only the half nobody attacks. The planted log carries the SAME principal on purpose, because a foreign one would be refused by the principal check and would red this cell without proving anything about the link.

mutations.name: S11 the log inside a real thread directory is read without checking it is a real file
mutations.note: The entry check clears the directory and stops there. Without this the guard is one level short rather than absent: a real thread directory holding a linked wal.json reaches the same foreign log by one more hop. The lstat is the graded layer because it is the portable one; O_NOFOLLOW behind it closes the check-to-open window, which no cell in this suite can reach.
